algorithm: For each bias type in config.bias_types that has patterns (unknown types are skipped silently). Iteration order is that of a Python set and is not stable; compare detected_biases as a set.

deobfuscated = text with each deobfuscation substitution applied to every occurrence, in the order listed. normalised = deobfuscated with every character matching normalisation_regex replaced by a space.
For each pattern in order: find all matches (case-insensitive) in the original text; if none, in deobfuscated; if none, in normalised. Append each match's full matched text, in order.
For each keyword in order: append the keyword itself if \b<escaped keyword>\b is found in text.lower().
score per type = scoring.formula. bias_scores has an entry for every checked type (0.0 when nothing matched); patterns_matched only for types that matched.
detected_biases = types with score >= threshold. has_bias = any. max_score = max of bias_scores, 0.0 when empty.
block_on_detection does not change the detector result (there is no blocked field); it only affects span annotation.

scoring.formula: 0.0 when nothing matched, else min(base_score + min(count_of_DISTINCT_matched_strings * per_unique_match, match_score_cap), total_score_cap)

algorithm: factual_claim_count = total number of matches of every factual_claim_pattern (case-insensitive, so [A-Z] also matches lowercase). A substring matched by two patterns counts twice.
hedge_words_count = sum over hedge_words of matches of \b<word>\b in text.lower(); forced to 0 when check_hedging is false.
citation_count = total matches of every confidence_markers pattern (case-insensitive); forced to 0 when check_citations is false.
score starts at 0.0. If factual_claim_count > 0: ratio = citation_count / factual_claim_count; ratio == 0 adds 0.4, ratio < 0.3 adds 0.2.
words = text split on whitespace. If there are words and hedge_words_count / len(words) > 0.1, add 0.3.
Add 0.1 for each inline specific_patterns entry found (case-insensitive). Cap at 1.0.

Indicators, in this order: 'specific_claims_without_citations' when factual_claim_count > 0 and citation_count == 0; 'high_uncertainty_language' when hedge_words_count > 3; 'absolute_statements' when any absolute word occurs as a whole word and citation_count == 0.

unsupported_claims (only with the first indicator): for every factual-claim match, in pattern order then match order, search the text case-insensitively for [^.!?]* + <regex-escaped match text> + [^.!?]*[.!?] and take the first hit, whitespace-stripped; matches with no hit are skipped; keep the first 3. A decimal point ends a 'sentence', so '$45.7 billion' yields '...earned $45.' for one of its two matches.

Internal contradiction: split text on [.!?]+; with fewer than 2 pieces, none. Per piece (lower-cased) collect (subject, value) pairs with the inline number_pattern; the same subject with a different value is a contradiction. Otherwise, if any contradiction_marker occurs and the text contains at least two DISTINCT number strings, it is a contradiction. A contradiction adds indicator 'context_contradiction' and 0.3 (capped at 1.0).

Context contradiction (only when context is non-empty): same subject with a different number in context and text; or exactly one of context/text contains a negation pattern and they share more than 2 distinct words of 4+ ASCII letters. Adds 0.3 again (capped), and the indicator if not already present.
has_hallucination = score >= threshold.
On a span the PROMPT is passed as context (plus gen_ai.context / gen_ai.retrieval.documents / gen_ai.rag.context when present).
If config.enabled is false: has_pii=false, original_text=text, nothing else.

For each fallback pattern, in fallback_pattern_order, whose entity_type is in config.entity_types: every non-overlapping regex match (Python re.finditer, no flags) becomes an entity {type, start, end, score, text}. start/end are offsets in Unicode code points, end exclusive.
Then for each config.custom_patterns entry in insertion order: the value is either a regex string (score 0.8) or {regex, score}.
Patterns are independent, so one substring can be reported under several types (a 16-digit card also matches IN_AADHAAR; a 10-digit number starting 6-9 is both PHONE_NUMBER and IN_PHONE).
config.threshold and config.allow_list are NOT applied on this path; they are only passed to Presidio.
has_pii = at least one entity. score = max entity score, 0.0 when none. entity_counts = count per type.

mode=redact and has_pii: process entities by start descending, replacing [start,end) with redaction_char repeated (end-start) times; then truncate to content_max_length characters when content_max_length > 0.
mode=block: blocked = has_pii.
original_text is null when has_pii and mode is not detect; otherwise the input.
For every injection type in type_order, for each pattern in order, append the full text of every case-insensitive match.
score per type = scoring.formula. injection_score = max over types.
injection_types = types with score >= threshold, in type_order. is_injection = any. blocked = block_on_detection and is_injection.
patterns_matched has an entry only for types that matched.

scoring.formula: 0.0 when nothing matched, else min(base_score + min(count_of_DISTINCT_matched_strings * per_unique_match, match_score_cap), total_score_cap)

algorithm: Topics checked = config.restricted_topics when it is a non-empty list, otherwise all topics in topic_order. Unknown topic names are skipped.

For each pattern in order, append the full text of every case-insensitive match. For each keyword in order, append the keyword if it is a SUBSTRING of text.lower() (no word boundary: 'harm' matches 'pharmacy').
score per topic = scoring.formula. detected_topics = topics with score >= threshold in checked order. max_score = max over checked topics.
blocked = block_on_detection and has_restricted_topic.

scoring.formula: 0.0 when nothing matched, else min(base_score + min(count_of_DISTINCT_matched_strings * per_unique_match, match_score_cap), total_score_cap)

toxicity.behaviour_without_a_backend: is_available() is false and detect() returns is_toxic=false, scores={}, max_score=0.0, toxic_categories=[], blocked=false for every input. The span processor then writes evaluation.toxicity.<prompt|response>.detected=false. There is no keyword or regex implementation to port.
toxicity.decision: category is toxic when score >= threshold; is_toxic = any category toxic
ml_backends: Google Perspective API (network; refused when allow_external_egress is false)

extraction: mixed. Pattern tables, word lists and config defaults are RUNTIME (class attributes and dataclass instances of the imported library). PII fallback regexes, scoring constants, the toxicity category maps, the bias substitutions and hallucination `inline_rule_data` are STATIC (read with ast from literals inside the detector methods, because they are locals). `algorithm` is prose written by hand from the source; eval_vectors.json is what verifies a port, not the prose.

regex_dialect.matching: re.finditer / re.findall semantics: leftmost, non-overlapping matches
regex_dialect.offsets: code points (not UTF-16 units, not bytes)
regex_dialect.unicode: Patterns are str patterns, so \w, \d, \s and \b are Unicode-aware: \d matches any Unicode decimal digit and \b treats non-ASCII letters as word characters.
